# Go jump CFG / RD contract (slice 2)

These files are parsed, never executed as Go. `design_goto.go` copies the design's
small goto probe. `jumps.go` covers forward/backward goto, labels on separate and
shared lines, jumps to an enclosing block, named and unnamed break/continue,
for/switch/select/type-switch targets, nested loops, final exits (with and without
defer), and a function consisting only of a goto. `edge_cases.go` adds direct
continue, range break, a labeled type switch, and a cross-case doubt control.

`base.jsonl` records all 27 Go fixtures (all Go U/D rows plus these four inputs)
on d63d3cbc, in the same worktree/runtime as head. It pins the complete public
DataFlow endpoint multiset, including byte spans, plus labels and RD/counter state.
`label_changes.jsonl` lists the 47 audited changes relative to those receipts;
`expected_stats.jsonl` gives the four changed files' counter/availability results.
The test applies only those explicit deltas: every other label, edge, and statistic
must stay identical to base. Goldens are inputs, never generated by the assertions.

`go_jump_cfg_targets` independently pins semantic destinations via comments.
`go_jump_labels_and_edge_keys` checks every changed label and the complete unchanged
edge multiset. Restoring the base production CFG/cache sources makes both tests
fail, with all 47 label obligations failing at RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 and 4.

The Go function-literal inventory gap is deliberately preserved: an outer goto
must resolve its own label and may not bind a same-name label inside a literal.
`nested_local` pins the absence of literal CFG ownership today. `noGoto` preserves
the original unused-label behavior. Unit tests also reject unresolved labels and
continue-to-switch/non-enclosing break labels; malformed Go is static recovery
input, not an assertion that those programs type-check.

Resolved jumps carry Structured provenance. Invented sequential cross-arm joins
remain flagged; the cross-case control remains cfg_incomplete. Go switch
header-to-case edges remain outside this slice.

`defer_exit.go` preserves doubt for a later write into an earlier defer argument,
while a normal break into a following defer reads the write exactly. Synthetic
function-exit dispatch has explicit GoDeferExit provenance and stays incomplete,
like return-to-defer; ordinary jumps keep Structured provenance.
